candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record supports metastatic Crohn disease: non-necrotizing granulomas with Langhans giant cells on biopsy, negative infectious workup, negative DIF, elevated anti-flagellin antibodies (Fla-X, A4-Fla2) on PROMETHEUS IBD sgi testing, family history of similar condition in son, and failure of adalimumab (suggesting severe/refractory CD). Hidradenitis suppurativa can present in intertriginous areas and may mimic this clinically, but its histopathology features follicular occlusion, abscess formation, and sinus tracts—not well-formed non-necrotizing granulomas with epithelioid histiocytes and Langhans giant cells. HS and metastatic CD are related differentials but represent incompatible diagnostic entities given the granulomatous histology and serologic findings here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a distinct inflammatory follicular occlusion disorder of intertriginous skin; metastatic Crohn disease is a non-contiguous cutaneous granulomatous manifestation of Crohn disease

case_quality_flags: Elevated anti-flagellin antibodies (Fla-X, A4-Fla2) are specific markers for Crohn disease and strongly support the reference diagnosis
Non-necrotizing granulomatous histology with negative infectious stains/cultures is a key discriminator favoring metastatic Crohn disease over HS
Family history of similar condition raises possibility of familial Crohn disease
